imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: The Good Father at the Bad Place. Cast/design continuity: A fictional father with dark cropped hair in a teal shirt, two individually distinct daughters: older child with dark bob and terracotta cardigan, smaller child with tied dark curls and ochre dress. Ordinary natural-history museum with one mechanical dinosaur model; later a small warm bedroom. No text, banners, logos, chase or monstrous creature.. CELL 0: Wide natural-history museum. Father enters beside his two daughters, gesturing enthusiastically toward a large dinosaur exhibit at a safe distance. Older daughter holds his free hand; smaller child stays beside his leg. Show both children’s separate uncertain expressions, feet planted in the museum space. CELL 1: Same museum and family. Dinosaur model has made one small forward lean, entirely within its exhibit. Older daughter points toward it, father turns his eyes to follow her finger, smaller daughter begins leaning backward. The dinosaur never chases or touches anyone. CELL 2: Both daughters move back toward father rather than fleeing through the museum. He bends his knees and lowers open arms to receive them, keeping balanced feet on the floor. Children retain separate faces and clothing. Fear is small and believable, not a gag or exaggerated screaming mask. CELL 3: Father crouches at his daughters’ eye level in a quiet museum corner, one small hand held securely while the other child stays close. His face is apologetic and attentive; neither child is pressured to smile at the exhibit. Dinosaur remains distant and static. CELL 4: Later at night in a modest bedroom. Older daughter lies under a soft blanket, reaching one small hand toward father as he notices from the bedside. Smaller child sleeps quietly in a second bed deeper in frame. No dinosaur toy gag or museum fantasy intrudes. CELL 5: Wide quiet bedroom. Father sits naturally on a sturdy chair beside older daughter’s bed, one hand resting gently near her offered hand, grounded feet and relaxed shoulders. Her body settles toward sleep. Smaller daughter stays asleep in her own bed; warm bedside lamp and steady ordinary presence. Editorial limit: Two daughters need separate readable reactions. No added dinosaur chase or frightened-child comedy. End on presence, not perfection.
